messages:
Maria G: quick check — thinking about route-level quotas for the model-routing gateway. two options: per-route quotas (e.g. embeddings.v1, chat.gpt-3.5) or tenant-wide quota that we tag by route in telemetry. tradeoffs?
Alex C: per-route = clearer cost attribution and easier to show per-route usage in console. but comes with more quota objects and mgmt complexity. also, more edge checks means more latency/RTT unless we cache. :thinking_face:
Samir: tenant-wide + tagging is simpler for enforcement but harder for rate limiting spikes per-route. if a single route floods, tenant-wide quota doesn't protect other routes. we’d need soft-rationing or dynamic weights.
Jordan K: console/UX angle — customers expect per-feature toggles. if we show per-route budgets in the Console and allow canary allocations, per-route quotas are more intuitive. but we could surface derived per-route metrics even if enforcement is tenant-wide.
Lee (eng-platform): technical ops: important to decide where the enforcement lives. options: 1) gateway-enforced per-request (fast fail at edge), 2) central quota service (consistent, single source of truth) with local cache tokens, 3) hybrid (gateway consults local token cache + central for refill).
Maria G: hybrid sounds promising. can we keep enforcement at edge for low-latency but reconcile with central to avoid drift?
Alex C: yes — implement token-bucket locally, refill policy from central quota service over gRPC streaming. central emits refill deltas for tenant-route pairs. gateway applies them immediately. glue: small control plane stream per gateway cluster.
Samir: that implies we need a stable {tenant,route} id in all requests. two approaches: put route in header (x-redwood-route) OR encode route claim into JWT. header is easier for internal clients and works for proxies. JWT is safer but means reissuing tokens when routes change.
Jordan K: header also makes console debugging easier — we can show ephemeral traces with the route label. can we standardize header + server-side validation?
Lee (eng-platform): agree. propose header + a lightweight signature check in gateway (HMAC using a key shared with control plane) so we can reject forged route headers from untrusted clients. pseudo: ```http
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <token>
x-redwood-route: chat.gpt-3.5
```
Alex C: one more cross-cutting: transport choice. if we lean on gRPC streaming for the refill/control plane, we get low-latency updates. but browser frontends still do REST/fetch. gateway must support both for ingest. Envoy does well with HTTP/2 + gRPC, but we also need a graceful fallback for legacy clients (transcoding?).
Samir: right — we've debated rest vs grpc before. for internal gateway-control-plane use gRPC for push signals. for user-facing APIs, keep RESTful JSON for simplicity, but ensure the gateway maps route metadata into the internal proto model so downstream services get typed info.
Jordan K: rollout story: want to expose a Console flow where product owners can allocate a percentage of tenant quota to routes (e.g., 70% chat, 30% embeddings) and do a canary at 5% traffic to a new route variant. telemetry needs to surface utilization, rejects, and refill recons.
Maria G: telemetry detail question — what labels do we need? tenant_id, route, model_version, region, backend_variant, and enforce_reason (local_vs_central).
Lee (eng-platform): +1. also emit token-cache-hits vs misses so we can tune TTLs.
Alex C: on metrics backend — OpenTelemetry with OTLP => backend (tempo/jaeger for traces, prometheus-compatible for counters). make sure we tag metrics with route so Console can roll up charts per-route.
Samir: alerting: create SLO: token-refill-lag < 200ms 99th. and a rate-limit-rejects SLI per-route.
infra-bot: deploy/ci: control-plane gRPC stream v1 deployed to canary cluster-3 at 2025-03-08T14:03:12Z :rocket:
Jordan K: next steps: 1) prototype header propagation + gateway HMAC check, 2) central quota service gRPC streaming API sketch, 3) Console UI mock showing per-route buckets and canary weight slider. i'll sketch the mock and post tomorrow.
Maria G: thanks — i'll draft an RFC for hybrid enforcement + header convention. tagging people: @Alex C @Samir @Lee (eng-platform) for early review. :thumbsup:
